Parcoords dimension objects

Source: R/zz-gen-parcoords.R
go_parcoords_dimension.Rd

The dimensions (variables) of the parallel coordinates chart. 2..60 dimensions are supported. The object for an element of the dimensions list of a parcoords trace (go_parcoords()). go_parcoords_dimension() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_parcoords_dimension(
  ...,
  constraintrange = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  multiselect = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  range = NULL,
  templateitemname = NULL,
  tickformat = NULL,
  ticktext = NULL,
  tickvals = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  visible = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one.

constraintrange

The domain range to which the filter on the dimension is constrained. Must be an array of `[fromValue, toValue]` with `fromValue <= toValue`, or if `multiselect` is not disabled, you may give an array of arrays, where each inner array is `[fromValue, toValue]`. Vector or list of up to 2 element(s).

label

The shown name of the dimension. String.

multiselect

Do we allow multiple selection ranges or just a single range? Logical.

name

When used in a template, named items are created in the output figure in addition to any items the figure already has in this array. You can modify these items in the output figure by making your own item with `templateitemname` matching this `name` alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). Has no effect outside of a template. String.

range

The domain range that represents the full, shown axis extent. Defaults to the `values` extent. Must be an array of `[fromValue, toValue]` with finite numbers as elements. Vector or list of 2 element(s).

templateitemname

Used to refer to a named item in this array in the template. Named items from the template will be created even without a matching item in the input figure, but you can modify one by making an item with `templateitemname` matching its `name`, alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). If there is no template or no matching item, this item will be hidden unless you explicitly show it with `visible: true`. String.

tickformat

Sets the tick label formatting rule using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: "%h" for half of the year as a decimal number as well as "%{n}f" for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, "2016-10-13 09:15:23.456" with tickformat "%H~%M~%S.%2f" would display "09~15~23.46" String.

ticktext

Sets the text displayed at the ticks position via `tickvals`. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

tickvals

Sets the values at which ticks on this axis appear. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

values

Dimension values. `values[n]` represents the value of the `n`th point in the dataset, therefore the `values` vector for all dimensions must be the same (longer vectors will be truncated). Each value must be a finite number. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

visible

Shows the dimension when set to `true` (the default). Hides the dimension for `false`. Logical.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_parcoords_dimension object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

go_parcoords(
  dimensions = list(go_parcoords_dimension(visible = TRUE))
)
#> <go_parcoords>
#> {
#>   "type": "parcoords",
#>   "dimensions": [
#>     {
#>       "visible": true
#>     }
#>   ]
#> }
#>
